rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the contribution. The requested hook was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/commit/84285312d8d9f22ee0042e709db114e5415dbdde and is present on current main as `middleware.workspace.handleApplyEdit`. Your handler can await `next(params)`, save the affected documents if the edit was applied, and return the result. Closing as completed; the first client release containing the hook has not been identified here. The fix shipped in release/client/10.0.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Adds a workspace.handleApplyEdit middleware hook. handleApplyWorkspaceEdit now routes every workspace/applyEdit request through it with a next() continuation, so clients can intercept the edits and act on them, such as saving afterwards. This is the capability the issue requested.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed analysis. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/commit/0217674defa6a05c3cc4f9936a68669b47173555: once a client is stopped and its output channel has been disposed, late logging—including the server process's exit message—no longer recreates the channel. The fix is included starting with `vscode-languageclient` 10.0.0-next.19 and in stable 10.0.0, so stopping the old client and creating its replacement should no longer leave an extra output entry from this path. The fix shipped in release/client/10.0.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff guards error/warn/info/debug with shouldLogToOutputChannel(), which skips logging once the client is Stopped and its channel was disposed. That blocks the reported post-stop exit-code log from recreating the output channel through the getter.

rows.title: Allow customizing the name of the option for enabling tracing
Support `isAI` property on `CodeAction`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the contribution. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/commit/62b3198a95ac9af13e04a27248b28951064546f9 and shipped in `vscode-languageclient` 10.0.0 with LSP 3.18 support. The protocol representation is `CodeAction.tags: [CodeActionTag.LLMGenerated]`; the client advertises `textDocument.codeAction.tagSupport` and converts that tag to VS Code's `isAI: true`, providing the marker used for the sparkle icon. Closing as completed. The fix shipped in release/client/10.0.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit adds a proposed CodeAction `tags` field with an LLMGenerated tag, a client tagSupport capability, and converters both ways that map the tag to and from vscode's `isAI`. This is the asCodeAction conversion the issue asks for.

Overflow value(exceeding uinteger) passed into jsonrpc  but still work
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This is a concrete case of the general LSP object validation layer tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/issues/695, so we're consolidating the request there. The formatting response containing Rust `u32::MAX` (`4294967295`, above LSP's `2147483647` maximum) is a useful example to retain, along with the requirement that validation be configurable to avoid unexpectedly changing existing behavior. This closes the duplicate request, not because bounds checking has been implemented.
rows.verifyEvidence: B asks for clearer errors (URI, server ID, range) when a handler rejects malformed diagnostics. A reports that out-of-range uinteger positions (u32::MAX) are accepted without any check, so B's error-reporting fix need not add uinteger bounds validation.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is now implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/commit/35409e7720f1edee1f70d0283fea33bbf6496055 and shipped with `vscode-languageclient` 10.1.2. The sending-response trace now includes `Request failed: <message> (<code>).` whenever the response contains an error, including when there is no `error.data`, so the rejected registration request will be clearly identified. Closing as completed. The fix shipped in release/client/10.1.2.
rows.verifyEvidence: When message.error is set, the diff now adds 'Request failed: <message> (<code>).' to the traceSendingResponse 'Sending response' line. That is exactly the missing -32602 code and message the report describes.

rows.title: Error handler unable to intercept and suppress error notification
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and the additional reconnection example. This falls within the broader request to let clients intercept all errors and control their presentation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/issues/1262. Closing this as a duplicate of that request, not as fixed.

The specific cases to retain are that `errorHandler.closed()` is skipped while the client is stopping, so `handled: true` cannot suppress the default notification, and that the automatic-restart failure path forces a dialog even when an extension subsequently reconnects successfully. The compatibility guidance here—making the additional interception opt-in—also belongs with that work.
rows.verifyEvidence: B asks for localization of unlocalized jsonrpc connection error strings; A asks that errorHandler be able to suppress the 'Connection to server got closed' notification during Stopping. Localizing messages wouldn't let clients suppress it.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional reports. The working-directory path still uses `.then(...).finally(...)`, but both directory-resolution branches normally return promises that support `finally`. Could someone share a minimal client/server repository and the steps that trigger this, or an affected-session diagnostic showing whether `Promise.prototype.finally` is present and whether the extension bundles or installs a Promise replacement? Please include the affected extension's `vscode-languageclient` version. That would help distinguish the startup code from an extension-host or bundling interaction without deleting preferences or extensions.
